candidates.statement: The provisions of this Chapter apply to the main body of the PSMF and its Annexes, including all supporting documentation, and shall be complied with in full. MAHs shall ensure that the PSMF is maintained in a manner that is accurate, complete, up to date, and readily accessible to the QPPV and the Authority always.
candidates.context: 2.2. Scope This Chapter applies to all Marketing Authorization Holders (MAHs) required to maintain a pharmacovigilance system. It covers all pharmacovigilance systems, including those that are shared between multiple MAHs or where activities are delegated to third parties. This Chapter 1s aligned with international best practices and makes reference to the Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module II: Pharmacovigilance System Master File (Revision 2) (EMA/816573/2011/Rev 2) .

candidates.statement: 2.4.1. The pharmacovigilance system master file provides an overview of the pharmacovigilance system put in place by the MAH and contributes to the appropriate management of and improvement(s) to the pharmacovigilance system. The PSMF shall reflect safety informa tion for medicinal products authorized in Nigeria. The PSMF shall contribute to the planning and conduct of audits by the MAH , fulfilment of supervisory responsibilities of the QPPV and inspections by NAFDAC. PSMF provides an overview of the Pharmacovigila nce system which may be requested and assessed by the Agency during marketing authorization application (s) or post authorization.

2.6.1. Marketing Authorization Holder s in Nigeria are required to maintain a pharmacovigilance system master file and submit to the Agency during application for Certificate of R egistration of a medicinal product, upon request, and upon update. The pharmacovigilance system master file shall be located either at the site in Nigeria where the Marketing Authorization Holder 's main pharmacovigilance activities are performed, or at the site in Nigeria where the qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance operates. Where the PSMF is stored in electronic form, the location stated must be a site where the data stored can be directly accessed.
candidates.context: 2.6. Maintenance of the Pharmacovigilance System Master File 2.6.2. Applicants for, and holders of, listings for traditional herbal medicinal products shall also be required to establish and maintain a Pharmacovigilance System Master File (PSMF).

candidates.statement: 2.7. 1. Transfer or delegation of responsibilities and activities concerning the master file shall be documented (see sections 2.18. and 2.35) and managed to ensure that the Marketing Authorization Holder fulfils their responsibilities. Since a specific QPPV ha s responsibility for the pharmacovigilance system, changes to the pharmacovigilance system master file shall also be notified to the QPPV in order to support their authority to make improvements to the system. The types of changes that shall be routinely a nd promptly notified to the QPPV are:
candidates.context: 2.7. Transfer of responsibility for the PSMF a. Updates to the PSMF or its location that are notified to the competent authorities .

candidates.statement: b. The addition of corrective and/or preventive actions to the pharmacovigilance system master file (e.g. following audits and inspections). The QPPV shall also be able to access information about deviations from the processes defined in the quality management system for pharmacovigilance .
candidates.context: a. Updates to the PSMF or its location that are notified to the competent authorities . c. Changes to content that fulfil the criteria for appropriate oversight of the pharmacovig ilance system (in terms of capacity, functioning , and compliance);

candidates.statement: 2.7.2. Any incoming QPPV must formally accept, in writing, the transfer of responsibility for the pharmacovigilance system. The QPPV shall also be able to ensure and verify that the Pharmacovigilance System Master File (PSMF) accurately and co nsistently reflects the current structure, processes, and activities of the pharmacovigilance system under his or her responsibility (see Chapter 1) .
candidates.context: g. Changes in arrangements for the provision of the PSMF to competent authorities 2.8. The R epresentation of P harmacovigilance S ystems

candidates.statement: 2.8.1. The pharmacovigilance system master file may describe the pharmacovigilance system for one or more medicinal products of the Marketing Authorization Holder . For different categories of medicinal products , the Marketing Authorization Holder may, if appropri ate, apply separate pharmacovigilance systems. Each of such systems shall be described in a separate pharmacovigilance system master file. Those files shall cumulatively cover all medicinal products of the Marketing Authorization Holder for which a Certifi cate of Registration has been issued.
candidates.context: 2.8. The R epresentation of P harmacovigilance S ystems 2.8.2. It is anticipated that there may be circumstances in which a single Marketing Authorization Holder may establish more than one pharmacovigilance system, e.g., specific systems for particular product types (vacci nes, consumer health , etc. ), or that the pharmacovigilance system may include products from more than one marketing authorization holder. In either case, a single and clearly defined specific system shall be in place to describe each system.

candidates.statement: 2.9.1. The pharmacovigilance system master file shall include documents to describe the pharmacovigilance system. The content of the pharmacovigilance system master file shall have the headings used in sections 2.1 0 to 2. 1 8 and shall reflect the global av ailability of safety information for medicinal products authorized in Nigeria. The content shall be indexed to allow for efficient navigation around the document.
candidates.context: 2.9. Content of a Pharmacovigilance System Master File (PSMF) 2.9.2. The main principle for the structure of the content of the pharmacovigilance system ma ster file is that the primary topic sections contain information that is fundamental to the description of pharmacovigilance system. Detailed information is required to fully describe the system, and, since this may change frequently, it shall be referred to and contained in the Annexes.

candidates.statement: 2. 1 2 . 2 Links with other organizations, such as co - marketing agreements and contracting of pharmacovigilance activities, shall be ou tlined. This may be in the form of a list/table to show the parties involved, the roles undertaken, and the concerned product(s). The list shall be organized according to service providers (e.g., medicinal information, auditors, patient support program providers, study data management, etc.), commercial arrangements (distributors, licensing partners, co - marketin g, etc.), and other technical providers (hosting of computer systems, etc.). Individual contractual agreements shall be made available at the request of the Agency or during inspection and audit and the list shall be provided in the Annexes.

candidates.statement: 2. 1 5 .1 An essential element of any pharmacovigilance system is that there are clear written procedures in place. Chapter 1 describes the required minimum set of written procedures for pharmacovigilance. A description of the procedural documentation available (st andard operating procedures, manuals, at global and/or national Level etc.), the nature of the data held (e.g. the type of case data retained for ICSRs) and an indication of how records are held (e.g. safety database, paper file at site of receipt) shall b e provided in the pharmacovigilance system master file.

candidates.statement: 2. 2 1 . 10 Documentation shall be maintained to support notifications and signatures related to the Pharmacovigilance System Master File (PSMF) as require d. Where an Annex contains no content, blank pages with headings are not necessary. However, all provided Annexes shall retain their designated format and numbering. This ensures that recipients of the PSMF understand that missing content is intentional.
